> something seems fishy about the strings inside `a:data`

Where can this be inspected from the coredump?
Frame 3 in your latest dump is the `copy()` call, so its `argvars` should be `a:data`.

```
(gdb) up 3
#3  0x00005585677a3b2d in f_copy (argvars=0x7ffdfc81f400, rettv=0x7ffdfc81faa0, fptr=0x0) at ../src/nvim/eval.c:7584
warning: Source file is more recent than executable.
7584	  var_item_copy(NULL, &argvars[0], rettv, false, 0);
(gdb) p argvars
$1 = (typval_T *) 0x7ffdfc81f400
(gdb) p *argvars
$2 = {v_type = VAR_LIST, v_lock = VAR_UNLOCKED, vval = {v_number = 94031511092928, v_special = (unknown: 1792081600), v_float = 4.6457739257555811e-310, 
    v_string = 0x55856ad0fec0 "\020\370\064k\205U", v_list = 0x55856ad0fec0, v_dict = 0x55856ad0fec0, v_partial = 0x55856ad0fec0}}
```

What does it mean?

According to the Neomake log from before the crash it ran the flake8 maker, and that should have returned no output, i.e. `a:data` should have been `['']`.

Reminded me of https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/5889 btw.
It's a list item, so you need to inspect v_list

```
(gdb) p *argvars.vval.v_list
$3 = {lv_first = 0x55856b34f810, lv_last = 0x55856c4b9f00, lv_refcount = 2, lv_len = 0, lv_watch = 0x0, lv_idx = 0, lv_idx_item = 0x0, lv_copyID = 0, lv_copylist = 0x0, 
  lv_lock = VAR_UNLOCKED, lv_used_next = 0x55856c4812d0, lv_used_prev = 0x60}
```

Does `lv_len = 0` mean that it is an empty list and not `['']` as I was expecting?
That would be my take.  You stated that the tool should have returned no output, so why do you expect the list to be populated?

body: Granted, your code shouldn't cause a crash, it should just do nothing.

There is always an empty line on stdout (for normal tools?!).

Running the following will output `[12, [''], 'stdout']`:

```vim
fun! F(...)
  echom string(a:000)
endfun
call jobstart("flake8 /dev/null", {'on_stdout': function('F')})
```

This is true for using `['true']` as the command, too.

> There is always an empty line on stdout (for normal tools?!).

No.

```
$ true | od -x
0000000
```

But at least from how Neovim sees it then, according to `call jobstart(['true'], {'on_stdout': {->execute('echom string(a:000)', 1)}})` which says `[9, [''], 'stdout']`.  That is another issue though.

Vim is silent / does not trigger the callback, also for flake8, using `call job_start(['flake8', '/dev/null'], {'callback': {->execute('echom string(a:000)', 1)}})`.
